description: Michael J. Heney (1864-1910), Canadian-Irish railway contractor. Built the White Pass & Yukon Route over the Coast Mountains from Skagway, and later the Copper River & Northwestern. Known as 'the Irish Prince'. Photographed here in early middle age in a wool three-piece suit with a high starched collar.
structural_anchor: A white man in his early forties of medium-heavy build, seen from the chest up. Broad squarish skull with a high wide forehead; dark hair worn short and swept back from a receding hairline that has retreated at both temples, leaving a blunt widow's peak. Straight strong nose with a broad bridge. Deep-set eyes under level brows, the lids heavy and slightly hooded, with pronounced shadow beneath. Full but firmly set mouth, corners level or faintly down. Clean-shaven throughout. Heavy square jaw and a thick neck; a fleshy chin with a soft crease beneath it. Ears set close and fairly large. Complexion weathered rather than fine. Period wardrobe: a heavy wool jacket with wide notched lapels over a waistcoat, a high stiff white collar, and a dark loosely knotted tie.
notes: Real historical figure. The anchor describes his documented likeness rather than a generic period engineer, so illustrated coverage reads as Heney. Spike A measures which framings can hold this identity; face-forward close-ups are the hardest case and should be treated as unproven until measured.
